title: Lolita
author: Vladimir Nabokov
summary: Humbert Humbert, an educated European, recounts from prison his obsession with a twelve-year-old girl and the cross-country journey that followed. His elegant, self-justifying narration is the book's trap.
readIf: you want a landmark of unreliable narration and ornate prose and can face a deeply disturbing narrator.
skipIf: depictions of child sexual abuse are something you cannot read, even when the narrator is condemned.

pairings.reason: Another literary novel narrated by someone who is charming, complicit and unreliable about a crime.
Lets you sit inside an amoral, intelligent mind, in a faster and more thriller-like way.
A modern, plot-heavy take on narrators who control the story they tell.
